name: Thirumakottai Temple
description: Thirumakottai Temple is a renowned temple attraction in Tiruvarur district, celebrating the cultural heritage, regional architecture, and scenic attractions of Tamil Nadu.

name: Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple
description: Built in 1035 CE by Emperor Rajendra Chola I to commemorate his victorious military march to the sacred River Ganges, a UNESCO World Heritage site and architectural twin to Thanjavur's Brihadeeswarar Temple, featuring a graceful 55-meter concave vimana, a colossal 13.5-foot monolithic Shiva Lingam (largest in South India), and exquisite stone carvings of Saraswati and Shiva-Parvati.

name: Karaivetti Bird Sanctuary Ariyalur
description: Covering 453.7 hectares around an expansive freshwater irrigation tank in Ariyalur district, designated as an international Ramsar Wetland site in January 2024, recognized as one of the largest freshwater bird sanctuaries in South India, hosting over 50,000 birds and serving as the premier wintering ground for the highest concentration of Bar-headed Geese in the state.

name: Alamparai Fort & Coastal Backwaters
description: Constructed in 1735 CE during the Mughal era under Nawab Dost Ali Khan of Arcot, an evocative 15-acre red-brick sea-fort jutting directly into the backwater estuary of the Bay of Bengal near Kadappakkam, featuring 100-meter-long sea-facing ramparts, watchtowers, and a 100-meter boat jetty once used for exporting silk and salt to international traders.

name: Arignar Anna Zoological Park
description: The official designated zoological research and conservation institution in Vandalur housing over 2,500 species of wild flora and fauna, noted for its active captive breeding programs for endangered species.

name: Arjuna's Penance (Descent of the Ganges)
description: Carved in the mid-7th century CE under the Pallava dynasty in Mamallapuram, a breathtaking UNESCO World Heritage open-air rock relief measuring an astounding 96 by 43 feet (29 by 13 meters) across two colossal pink granite boulders, depicting the cosmic descent of the holy river Ganges from heaven to earth brought by Sage Bhagiratha's severe penance, featuring over 100 celestial beings, life-size wild elephants, flying Gandharvas, and naturalistic animals.

name: Covelong (Kovalam) Beach & Surfing Point
description: Situated 40 km south of Chennai on the East Coast Road, an ancient port town developed by Nawab Saadat Ali of Carnatic and later a Dutch and French trading settlement, transformed into India's premier surfing capital, famous for the Covelong Point Surf School, consistent right-hand point break waves, the annual Covelong Surf Music & Yoga Festival, and the 18th-century Catholic Church of Our Lady of Carmel.

name: DakshinaChitra Heritage Museum
description: Spread across 10 lush coastal acres overlooking the Bay of Bengal on East Coast Road in Muttukadu, established in 1996 by the Madras Craft Foundation, a world-class living history museum containing 18 authentic traditional vernacular houses from Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, and Andhra Pradesh that were systematically dismantled, transported, and meticulously reconstructed by master craftsmen.

name: Hidden Lake
description: A secluded turquoise water-filled abandoned granite quarry nestled amidst the rugged rocky hills of Tirusulam near Chennai Airport.

name: Kamakshi Temple
description: A revered and vibrant temple dedicated to Goddess Sri Kamakshi in Sembakkam (Tambaram area), noted for its traditional Dravidian vimana and spiritual rituals.

name: Krishna's Butterball Mahabalipuram
description: Perched on a smooth 45-degree granite hillside in Mamallapuram, an astounding 250-tonne precariously balanced giant granite boulder rising 20 feet high and 16 feet wide, known traditionally as Vaan Irai Kal (Stone of the Sky God) and Krishna's Butterball, which has defied gravity for over 1,200 years on a minuscule contact surface less than 2 feet wide despite multiple royal attempts by Pallava kings and British governors to dislodge it with teams of elephants.

name: Madras Crocodile Bank Trust & Herpetology Centre
description: Established in 1976 by legendary conservationist Romulus Whitaker across 8.5 acres on the East Coast Road (ECR), recognized as one of the world's foremost reptile zoos and research institutions, housing over 2,400 reptiles across 14 of the world's 23 crocodile species (including the critically endangered Gharial and saltwater crocodile), Komodo dragons, Aldabra giant tortoises, and an Irula venom extraction demonstration centre.

name: Mahishasuramardini Cave Temple Mahabalipuram
description: Carved on a rocky granite hillock in Mamallapuram near the historic lighthouse, celebrated as one of the finest rock-cut cave temples of the Pallava golden age (mid-7th century CE), famous worldwide for two monumental opposing wall relief panels: one depicting Goddess Durga riding a ferocious lion in dynamic battle against the buffalo-headed demon Mahishasura, and the opposite showing Lord Vishnu reclining in cosmic sleep (Anantasayana) upon the serpent Adisesha.

name: Mamallapuram Tiger Cave (Saluvankuppam)
description: Located on the sandy coastline in Saluvankuppam 5 km north of Mamallapuram, an extraordinary 8th-century open-air rock-cut pavilion carved out of an isolated coastal boulder under Pallava King Rajasimha, featuring an arched cave sanctum framed by a dramatic semicircular crown of 11 ferocious sculpted Yali (lion/tiger) heads facing the sea.

name: Muttukadu Backwaters & Boat House
description: Formed by the broad estuary of the Buckingham Canal and Kovalam creek meeting the Bay of Bengal on the scenic East Coast Road (ECR), a sprawling coastal backwater lagoon developed by Tamil Nadu Tourism Development Corporation (TTDC) into a premier water sports destination offering speedboating, water scooters, rowboats, and pedal boats.

name: Pancha Rathas (Five Rathas) Mahabalipuram
description: Dating to the late 7th century CE during the reign of Pallava King Narasimhavarman I (Mamalla), an extraordinary UNESCO World Heritage ensemble of five monolithic rock-cut shrines carved out of single pink granite boulders in situ, named after the Pandavas (Dharmaraja, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula-Sahadeva) and Draupadi, accompanied by life-sized monolithic sculptures of an elephant, lion, and Nandi bull.

name: Sadras Dutch Fort & Coastal Cemetery
description: Constructed in 1612 CE by the Dutch East India Company on the Coromandel Coast 16 km south of Mamallapuram, a remarkably intact coastal fortress built for the muslin cloth trade, featuring grand brick ramparts, watchtowers, an ancient bell tower, a warehouse, and a Dutch cemetery with 19 exquisitely carved granite armorial headstones dating from 1620 to 1769.

name: Shore Temple & Mahabalipuram Monuments
description: Constructed in 700-728 CE under Pallava King Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) overlooking the Bay of Bengal, one of the oldest structural stone temples of Southern India, featuring five-storey granite towers and carved Nandi bulls.

name: Vandalur Zoo
description: The popular local moniker for Arignar Anna Zoological Park, India's first public zoo (founded 1855) and one of the largest in Asia, sprawling over 1,500 acres of natural scrub forest.

name: Vedanthangal Bird Sanctuary Chengalpattu
description: Covering 74 acres around a freshwater wetland in Chengalpattu district, celebrated as the oldest water bird sanctuary in India protected by local villagers since 1798 and formally established in 1936, designated as an international Ramsar Wetland site in 2022, hosting over 40,000 migratory waterfowl annually including Painted Storks, Spot-billed Pelicans, Grey Herons, and Eurasian Spoonbills.

name: Adyar Banyan Tree
description: A 450-year-old historic banyan tree spanning roughly 40,000 square feet within the tranquil campus of the Theosophical Society on the Adyar River banks.

name: Anna University
description: Historic premier technical university established on a leafy 185-acre campus in Guindy, featuring iconic heritage red-brick Indo-Saracenic buildings of the College of Engineering, Guindy (CEG, founded 1794).

name: BSR Mall
description: A premier neighborhood shopping and entertainment complex located in Thoraipakkam on the Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR) IT corridor.

name: Chennai Rail Museum Villivakkam
description: Spread across 6.5 acres adjacent to the Integral Coach Factory (ICF) in Villivakkam, an enchanting railway heritage park and museum displaying vintage working steam locomotives, wooden heritage saloons, royal inspection coaches, a rare 1895 Fowler steam plough, indoor art galleries displaying historic railway signals, and a joyful toy train ride winding through lush gardens.

name: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Park
description: A well-maintained civic park along EVR Periyar Salai featuring manicured green lawns, shaded walkways, children's play area, and outdoor fitness amenities.

name: ECR Beach
description: The wide, serene coastal beach corridor along the East Coast Road in Akkarai and Panaiyur, renowned for golden sands, refreshing sea breeze, and coastal villas.

name: Elliot's Beach
description: Popularly known as Bessy Beach, it forms the southern end of the Marina coastline in Besant Nagar, famed for the Karl Schmidt Memorial and vibrant food culture.

name: Fort Museum Fort St. George Chennai
description: Housed inside the historic 1795 Exchange Building within Fort St. George, an extraordinarily rich historical museum managed by ASI across three floors, displaying rare British East India Company colonial artifacts, French war trophies, original portraits of British royalty, and the historic first National Flag of Independent India hoisted at Fort St. George on 15 August 1947.

name: Golden Beach
description: Famed beach frontage associated with VGP Golden Beach, known for its pristine golden shoreline, iconic statues, adventure park rides, and beach cultural events.

name: Government Museum Egmore Chennai
description: Established in 1851 across 16 lush green acres in Egmore, recognized as the second oldest museum in India, celebrated globally for housing the world's finest and largest collection of ancient Chola Bronzes (including the iconic 10th-century Nataraja of Thiruvalangadu), 2nd-century BCE Amaravati Buddhist marble sculptures, Roman coins, and the Connemara Public Library.

name: Governor's Bungalow
description: A historic British-era colonial beachfront retreat along the Besant Nagar coastline historically utilized by Madras Governors for seaside convalescence.

name: Guindy National Park
description: A 2.7-square-kilometer protected reserve in the heart of Chennai, one of the world's few national parks situated entirely within a metropolitan city, sheltering spotted deer, endangered blackbucks, and tropical dry evergreen flora.

name: IIT Madras
description: India's premier institute of technology set amidst a 630-acre natural deciduous forest enclave adjoining Guindy National Park, home to wild spotted deer and blackbucks.

name: Iskcon Temple
description: The largest Radha Krishna temple in Tamil Nadu, spread over 1.5 acres on the East Coast Road (ECR), featuring exquisite traditional South Indian and contemporary architecture.

name: Kapaleeshwarar Temple Mylapore
description: Constructed originally in the 7th century CE by the Pallavas and rebuilt in the 16th century by Vijayanagara rulers in Mylapore, the quintessential spiritual and cultural landmark of Chennai, featuring a rainbow-colored 120-foot eastern Rajagopuram covered in sculpted stucco deities, the shrine of Goddess Karpagambal worshipping Shiva in the form of a peacock (Mayil), and a massive sacred temple tank.

name: Madras High Court Heritage Complex Chennai
description: Constructed in 1892 CE under the architectural direction of J. W. Brassington and Henry Irwin in George Town, recognized as the second largest judicial complex in the world after the Royal Courts of Justice in London, featuring majestic Indo-Saracenic red-brick arches, stained glass, minarets, and the 175-foot original Madras Lighthouse tower rising over the central dome.

name: Marina Beach
description: World's second longest natural urban beach, stretching roughly 12 kilometers along the Bay of Bengal, iconic for its expansive sands, historical statues, and bustling carnival atmosphere.

name: Matsya Narayana Temple
description: A serene open-air seaside temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu's Matsya (fish) avatar, managed by Chinmaya Mission along the scenic shores of Uthandi on ECR.

name: Parthasarathy Temple Triplicane
description: Constructed in the 8th century CE by Pallava King Narasimhavarman I and expanded by Chola and Vijayanagara kings in Triplicane, one of the oldest Vaishnavite Divya Desams in Chennai, famous as the only temple where Lord Krishna is depicted as 'Parthasarathy' (charioteer of Arjuna in the Mahabharata) sporting a distinguished moustache, bearing facial arrow scars from the Kurukshetra war, and without his Sudarshana Chakra.

name: Perarignar Anna Museum
description: Dedicated museum at the Anna Memorial complex on the Marina beachfront honoring C. N. Annadurai, featuring photographs, books, speeches, and personal artifacts.

name: Perungudi Lake
description: A scenic freshwater urban lake spread across 57 acres in Perungudi along the IT corridor, rejuvenated with walking bunds and bird roosting islands.

name: Phoenix Marketcity
description: One of the largest shopping malls in South India, spanning over 1 million square feet in Velachery, featuring hundreds of global lifestyle brands, luxury retail, IMAX cinema, and fine dining.

name: San Thome Basilica Chennai
description: Constructed originally in the 16th century by Portuguese explorers and rebuilt in 1896 by the British in graceful Neo-Gothic architecture, recognized as one of only three churches in the world built directly over the tomb of an original Apostle of Jesus Christ (along with St. Peter's Basilica in Vatican City and Santiago de Compostela in Spain), featuring a 183-foot soaring spire, an underground crypt chapel, and a museum holding the holy relic bone.

name: Semmozhi Poonga Chennai
description: Opened in 2010 by the Tamil Nadu Horticulture Department across 20 acres on Cathedral Road near the Gemini Flyover, recognized as Chennai's premier modern botanical garden, featuring 22 specialized theme gardens including a Bonsai garden, herbal garden, aroma garden, butterfly garden, vertical green walls, an artificial duck pond, and over 500 species of rare exotic plants sourced globally.

name: St. Mary's Church Fort St. George
description: Consecrated on 28 October 1680 inside Fort St. George, celebrated as the oldest surviving Anglican church in India and the entire Asian continent east of Suez, constructed with a unique 4-foot-thick bomb-proof curved masonry roof designed to withstand artillery bombardment during the Anglo-French wars, featuring the marriage registers of Robert Clive and Elihu Yale (benefactor of Yale University).

name: Taj Wellington Mews
description: India's first all-women managed luxury hospitality residence by IHCL, set in Chennai's OMR IT corridor, boasting LEED-certified eco-architecture and fine dining.

name: Theosophical Society Adyar Chennai
description: Established in 1882 by Helena Blavatsky and Colonel Henry Steel Olcott on the southern banks of the Adyar River in Chennai, an expansive 260-acre forested estate dedicated to universal brotherhood and comparative religion, functioning as an ecological sanctuary with over 300 species of trees, migratory bird habitats, and the world-famous 450-year-old Great Banyan Tree whose canopy spans over 40,000 square feet.

name: Thiruvalluvar Nagar Beach
description: A quiet, clean coastal sandy beach strip extending south from Thiruvanmiyur Beach, celebrated for sunrise views and an uncluttered natural shoreline.

name: Thousand Lights Mosque Chennai
description: Constructed in 1810 CE by Nawab Umdat-ul-Umrah of the Carnatic on Anna Salai in Chennai, the principal religious and cultural hub for the Shia Muslim community of Tamil Nadu, celebrated for its striking multi-domed Indo-Saracenic architecture with twin 64-foot minarets, named because exactly 1,000 oil lamps were traditionally lit to illuminate the expansive assembly hall.

name: Vadapalani Murugan Temple Chennai
description: Constructed in 1890 around a simple thatch hut consecrated by devotee Annaswami Nayakar in Vadapalani, transformed over a century into one of Chennai's most frequented and revered temples of Lord Murugan (Vadapalani Andavar), famous for its 108-foot eastern Rajagopuram depicting the 108 Bharatnatyam dance poses, and celebrated as the premier venue for traditional Hindu weddings in the city.

name: World Trade Centre
description: A premier 28-storey twin-tower commercial development on Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR), representing the modern technological and corporate skyline of Chennai.

name: Writer's Café
description: An inspiring community cafe and bookstore operated in partnership with the International Foundation for Crime Prevention and Victim Care (PCVC), employing burn survivors while serving artisanal Swiss confectionery and European fare.

name: Adiyogi Shiva Statue
description: Recognized by Guinness World Records as the world's largest bust sculpture, towering 112 feet tall, representing Shiva as the first yogi (Adiyogi) against the dramatic Velliangiri Mountain range.

name: Aliyar Dam & Reservoir Pollachi
description: Constructed between 1959 and 1969 across the Aliyar River near Pollachi at the very foot of the Anamalai Hills, an imposing 81-meter-high masonry and earthen dam that forms a glittering reservoir on the scenic Pollachi-Valparai road, featuring manicured hillside botanical gardens, a mini-aquarium, children's park, and pedal boating.

name: Anamalai Tiger Reserve (Top Slip & Sethumadai)
description: Spanning 958 square kilometers across the rugged tropical rainforests of the Anamalai Hills, formerly known as Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary, a vital tiger and elephant reserve harboring over 30 Royal Bengal tigers, Lion-tailed macaques, Indian leopards, and great hornbills, with its principal eco-tourism hub at Top Slip famed for jungle safaris and bamboo rafting.

name: Arulmigu Sri Eachanari Vinayagar Temple
description: Dating back to 1500 CE during the Madurai Nayak era, enshrining a magnificent 6-foot-tall monolithic idol of Lord Ganesha, originally being transported from Madurai to Perur.

name: Bharathiar University
description: Named after visionary Tamil national poet Subramania Bharati, a sprawling 1,000-acre green campus established in 1982 at the base of the Marudhamalai hills.

name: Bheeman Immovable Stone
description: A gigantic, mysteriously balanced natural granite boulder perched along the steep mountain path of the Velliangiri hills, linked in local lore to the Pandava prince Bhima.

name: Birla Waterfall
description: A picturesque, perennial mountain waterfall cascading through the lush green tea slopes of the Birla Tea Estate in the Anamalai Hills of Valparai.

name: Black Thunder Water Theme Park
description: Spanning 75 acres at the foot of the Nilgiri Hills in Mettupalayam, one of India's premier water theme parks featuring giant wave pools, reckless river rapids, and high-speed water slides.

name: Carver Marsh Statue (Kavarkal Estate)
description: A historic bronze memorial statue overlooking the misty Kavarkal tea estate, honoring Carvar Marsh, the pioneering British planter who first introduced tea cultivation to the Anamalai Hills in the 1890s.

name: Central Library Coimbatore
description: The District Central Library of Coimbatore, housing hundreds of thousands of rare books, historical archives, Tamil literature volumes, and digital reference sections.

name: Chinna Kalar Waterfall
description: Located in Chinnakallar, famously known as the 'Cherrapunji of South India' for recording the third highest rainfall in India, featuring a gushing mountain waterfall and suspension bridge.

name: Cross Cut Road Shopping
description: The commercial heartbeat of Coimbatore in Gandhipuram, famed throughout South India for massive multi-storey silk emporiums, traditional jewelry palaces, and electronic markets.

name: Dhyanalinga Meditation and Yoga Centre
description: A profound, non-religious meditative space established by Sadhguru at the Isha Yoga Center in the Velliangiri foothills, featuring a massive ellipsoid dome housing a 13-foot granite linga sanctified with seven chakras.

name: Diwan Bahadur Road (DB Road) Shopping
description: Coimbatore's premier tree-lined high-street shopping boulevard in R.S. Puram, celebrated for upscale designer silk boutiques, gold jewelers, and authentic South Indian vegetarian eateries like Annapoorna.

name: Ernatica Sea World Amusement Park
description: An indoor marine world exhibit featuring glass-tunnel fish tanks, exotic saltwater fish, coral reefs, and educational marine biodiversity displays.

name: Exotic Bird Park
description: An interactive walk-through aviary housing exotic bird species from across five continents, including macaws, cockatoos, toucans, lories, and rainbow lorikeets.

name: Gass Forest Museum Coimbatore
description: Established in 1902 by British forest conservator Horace Archibald Gass on the lush Forest College campus in Coimbatore, celebrated as the very first government forestry museum in India, housing over 10,000 rare historical natural history exhibits including taxidermy specimens of leopards and tigers, complete elephant skeletons, rare timber cross-sections, and indigenous tribal hunting tools.

name: Gedee Car Museum
description: Founded by legendary industrialist and inventor G.D. Naidu, South India's premier vintage automobile museum showcasing over 100 impeccably restored historic automobiles from Germany, Britain, France, America, and Japan.

name: Gedee Science Museum
description: An inspiring interactive science center dedicated to legendary Indian inventor G.D. Naidu ('Edison of India'), showcasing working engineering inventions, physics experiments, and agricultural machines.

name: Government Arts College
description: Established in 1852, one of the oldest higher education institutions in South India, featuring magnificent stone Indo-Saracenic colonial buildings and centenary banyan trees.

name: Iraichal Parai Waterfall
description: Originating from the Nadumalai river, a cascading waterfall flowing over expansive granite rocks nestled within the quiet tea estates near Valparai town.

name: Isha Yoga Temple
description: The sacred spiritual complex comprising Linga Bhairavi Temple, Suryakund, and Chandrakund subterranean energy pools filled with energized mercury lingams.

name: Kovai Kutralam Waterfall
description: A magnificent perennial waterfall created by the Siruvani River coursing through a rocky gorge in the protected reserve forests of the Western Ghats.

name: Marudamalai Murugan Temple Coimbatore
description: Perched at 2,000 feet atop a lush granite hill in the Western Ghats 12 km west of Coimbatore, a 1,200-year-old temple of Lord Murugan (Marudachalamurthy) constructed during the Kongu Chola period, surrounded by thousands of rare Ayurvedic medicinal plants and sacred natural springs (Maruda Thirtham), associated with 12th-century mystic Siddhar Pambatti.

name: Marudhamalai Temple
description: An ancient 12th-century hilltop temple dedicated to Lord Murugan (Dhandayuthapani), perched atop a scenic hillock of the Western Ghats rich in medicinal marudham trees.

name: Masaniamman Temple
description: A highly revered Hindu temple on the Aliyar river banks in Anaimalai, enshrining a unique 15-foot reclining stucco idol of Goddess Masaniamman with four hands holding sacred emblems.

name: Monkey Waterfalls
description: A natural perennial cascade situated on the Pollachi-Valparai ghat road in the Anamalai Tiger Reserve foothills, surrounded by dense rocky cliff walls and wild evergreen flora.

name: Narasipuram Multi Step Waterfall (Vaidehi Falls)
description: Locally known as Vaidehi Falls, a pristine multi-stepped forest cascade nestled in the dense Western Ghats reserve forest near Narasipuram village.

name: Perur Pateeswarar Temple
description: Built by Chola monarch Karikala in the 2nd century CE along the Noyyal River, famed for the Kanaka Sabha (Golden Hall) with breathtaking pillars depicting Shiva's cosmic dance.

name: Sholayar Dam Lake Viewpoint
description: Constructed in 1965 as part of the Parambikulam Aliyar Project, this massive high-altitude reservoir sits at 3,500 feet, boasting one of the highest masonry dams in Asia.

name: Singanallur Lake
description: A 288-acre natural urban wetland declared as an Urban Biodiversity Conservation Zone, sheltering over 160 species of resident and migratory water birds, butterflies, and indigenous aquatic flora.

name: Siruvani Waterfall
description: The upper cascade of the Siruvani river nestled in the dense shola hills, acclaimed globally for producing naturally sweet drinking water.

name: St. Michael's Cathedral
description: Originally consecrated in 1867 and rebuilt in modern Gothic majesty, the seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Coimbatore featuring soaring towers and vibrant stained-glass murals.

name: Sungam Lake Boating (Valankulam Lake)
description: A revitalized Smart City waterfront on Valankulam Lake near Sungam, boasting illuminated wooden boardwalks, floating fountains, pedal boating, and landscaped evening food plazas.

name: Valparai Hill Station & 40 Hairpin Bends
description: Perched at 3,500 feet in the Anamalai Hills 65 km from Pollachi, reached via a thrilling mountain highway containing exactly 40 continuous hairpin bends, an untouched tea plateau surrounded by dense evergreen rainforests, free from commercial tourist noise, home to wild leopards, lion-tailed macaques, Indian gaurs, and magnificent viewpoints like Koolangal River and Sholayar Dam.

name: Valparai Market
description: The central market hub of the Valparai plateau where plantation workers, planters, and visitors congregate, famous for freshly processed teas, green cardamom, spices, and homemade bakery items.

name: Varadaraja Perumal Temple
description: A historic and spiritually revered temple dedicated to Lord Varadaraja Perumal in Peelamedu, celebrated for its sculpted stone gopuram and peaceful sanctum.

name: Velliangiri Sivan Hill Temple
description: Revered as 'Thenkailayam' (Kailash of the South), a self-manifested (Swayambhu) Shiva shrine perched at 5,833 feet atop the 7th hill of the Velliangiri range where Shiva performed the cosmic Ananda Tandava.

name: Velliangiri Temple Trail Trek
description: The arduous hiking trail traversing seven distinct Western Ghats peaks through dense tropical shola forests, rocky staircases, and windy alpine grasslands.

name: VOC Ground Amusement Park
description: A historic recreational civic park named after freedom fighter V.O. Chidambaram Pillai, featuring an amusement zone, miniature toy train, and lush garden walking tracks.

name: Pichavaram Mangrove Forest
description: Tucked away in the Cuddalore district of Tamil Nadu, the Pichavaram Mangrove Forest is an untouched haven of mangrove swamps, dense forests, and serene waterways. A vital habitat for diverse marine life, the forest boasts an enchanting world of mangrove trees, which filter freshwater from the sea, creating a unique ecosystem. With its winding water paths, Pichavaram is a nature lover's haven, where one can experience the unspoiled beauty of the mangrove ecosystem through guided boat tours, nature walks, and photography excursions.

name: Silver Beach Cuddalore
description: Stretching for kilometers along the Coromandel Coast in Devanampattinam 2 km from Cuddalore, celebrated as the second longest beach in Tamil Nadu and one of the longest natural beaches in Asia, separated from the town by the tranquil backwaters of the Uppanar River, famous for horse riding, water sports, and historical Fort St. David ruins.

name: Thillai Nataraja Temple Chidambaram
description: Constructed during the Chola dynasty, a magnificent 40-acre temple complex dedicated to Lord Shiva as Nataraja (the Cosmic Dancer), representing the element of space/ether (Akasha Lingam), famous for its gold-plated roof of the Chit Sabha and the mysterious 'Chidambara Rahasya'.

name: Hogenakkal Falls
description: Located on the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border, Hogenakkal Falls is a breathtaking spectacle of nature that has captivated the imagination of visitors for centuries. The falls, also known as 'Niagara of India', owe their origin to the Cauvery River, which flows from the Western Ghats and cascades down from a height of 50-100 feet over a series of rocky outcrops. The falls are a treat for nature lovers and adventure enthusiasts, with stunning views, serene surroundings, and a host of activities such as boat rides, nature walks, and bird watching.

name: Berijam Lake Kodaikanal
description: Situated 21 km from Kodaikanal town inside a strictly protected forest sanctuary at an elevation of 7,100 feet, a pristine 59-acre crescent-shaped mountain lake created in 1867 by the British, renowned for its crystal-clear non-polluted waters providing the drinking supply to Periyakulam, surrounded by dense Shola forests sheltering Indian gaurs, Nilgiri langurs, and rare orchids.

name: Bryant Park Kodaikanal
description: Constructed and landscaped in 1908 by British forest officer H. D. Bryant on the eastern edge of Kodaikanal Lake, a 20.5-acre manicured botanical paradise housing over 325 species of temperate trees, shrubs, and cacti, featuring a 160-year-old sacred Bodhi tree, an expansive rose garden with 740 varieties, an orchid glasshouse, and hosting the grand annual horticulture flower show in May.

name: Coaker's Walk Kodaikanal
description: Constructed in 1872 by Lieutenant Coaker along the steep mountain slopes 500 meters from Kodaikanal Lake, an iconic 1-kilometer pedestrian promenade winding along the edge of sheer cliffs, offering breathtaking aerial views of the Dolphin's Nose, Pambar River valley, Madurai plains, and the rare optical phenomenon 'Brocken Spectre' where a viewer's shadow is cast upon mist with a rainbow halo.

name: Green Valley View (Suicide Point) Kodaikanal
description: Situated 5.5 km from Kodaikanal Lake near the Kodaikanal Golf Club, formerly known as Suicide Point, a dramatic mountain precipice that drops an astonishing 5,000 feet (1,500 meters) straight down into the Vaigai River valley and reservoir, offering dizzying aerial panoramas of the surrounding Palani ranges, protected by high safety railings and surrounded by lush commercial markets.

name: Guna Caves (Devil's Kitchen) Kodaikanal
description: Discovered in 1821 by British officer B. S. Ward and originally named Devil's Kitchen, an eerie geological formation of deep rock crevices plunging over 500 feet into the mist-shrouded mountain abyss between Pillar Rocks, surrounded by surreal twisted root networks of ancient Shola pine trees, renamed 'Guna Caves' after Kamal Haasan filmed his cult 1991 movie here.

name: Kodaikanal Lake
description: Constructed in 1863 by Sir Vere Henry Levinge at an altitude of 7,500 feet in the Palani Hills of the Western Ghats, a magnificent 60-acre star-shaped artificial freshwater lake surrounded by deodars, kurinji bushes, and an encircling 5-km pedestrian path.

name: Kukkal Caves Kodaikanal
description: Perched at an elevation of 6,200 feet in Kukkal village 30 km from Kodaikanal, an extraordinary natural rock overhang that provided shelter to prehistoric humans and the indigenous Palaiyar hunter-gatherer tribe, featuring ancient rock art paintings on cave walls, surrounded by terraced carrot farms, high-altitude Shola grasslands, and a serene mountain lake.

name: Mannavanur Lake Kodaikanal
description: Located in the tranquil farming village of Mannavanur 35 km from Kodaikanal, an exceptionally picturesque high-altitude lake surrounded by rolling emerald grass meadows resembling the Scottish Highlands, managed alongside the Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute (CSWRI) where flocks of Bharat Merino and rabbit species roam freely.

name: Pillar Rocks Kodaikanal
description: Located 8 km from Kodaikanal lake, an awe-inspiring geological landmark consisting of three monumental vertical granite rock pillars soaring 400 feet (122 meters) straight up into the sky from the mountain cliff, separated by dramatic fissures, surrounded by manicured floral gardens and viewing pavilions maintained by Tamil Nadu Tourism.

name: Silver Cascade Falls Kodaikanal
description: Situated 8 km before Kodaikanal town on the main Laws Ghat road, a spectacular 180-foot (55 m) wide mountain waterfall formed by the overflow waters of the world-famous Kodaikanal Lake, crashing down over dark stepped basalt rocks into a foaming white spray that glistens like pure liquid silver.

name: Sirumalai Hill Station Dindigul
description: Rising 5,200 feet above sea level in the Eastern Ghats 25 km south of Dindigul, reached via a winding mountain road with 18 scenic hairpin bends, a tranquil, uncommercialized forested hill station famous worldwide for its sweet medicinal GI-tagged Sirumalai Hill Banana (Malai Vazhaipazham), lush coffee and spice plantations, and the Sanjeevi Hills legend.

name: Thalaiyar Falls (Rat Tail Falls) Dindigul
description: Plunging an astounding 975 feet (297 meters) over a vertical black rock precipice in the Palani Hills, the highest waterfall in Tamil Nadu and the 6th highest in India, appearing from afar across the Batlagundu-Kodaikanal ghat road as a striking slender white strip resembling a rat's tail against the dark forested cliff face.

name: Bhavanisagar Dam (Lower Bhavani Dam)
description: Constructed between 1948 and 1955 at the confluence of the Bhavani and Moyar Rivers, recognized as the second largest earthen dam in India and one of the largest in the world measuring an astonishing 8.08 kilometers in length, rising 40 meters high, featuring a beautiful landscaped park below the dam with musical dancing fountains and boat rides.

name: Kodiveri Waterfall and Dam
description: A 17th-century check dam built across the Bhavani River by the Kongu Chola kings, where river waters spill smoothly over stone weirs creating a gentle natural water park.

name: Kodumanal Archaeological Industrial Site
description: Located on the northern banks of the Noyyal River in Erode district, an extraordinarily rich 2,500-year-old industrial and trade center of the Sangam era mentioned in the classical Tamil text 'Pathitrupathu' as 'Kodumanam', famous for producing high-grade wootz steel for Damascus swords, thousands of semi-precious quartz, beryl, and carnelian beads, and Roman trade artifacts.

name: Sathyamangalam Tiger Reserve Erode
description: Encompassing 1,411 square kilometers of mixed deciduous and thorn scrub forest in Erode district, celebrated internationally with the TX2 global conservation award for doubling its wild tiger population to over 85 tigers, functioning as the vital ecological corridor linking the Western and Eastern Ghats, home to over 800 wild Asian elephants, leopards, and hyenas.

name: Ekambareswarar Temple Kanchipuram
description: Spanning 25 acres in the temple city of Kanchipuram, one of the five cosmic Pancha Bhoota Sthalams representing the element of Earth (Prithvi Lingam) molded by Goddess Parvati herself, famous for its colossal 59-meter (192 ft) entrance Rajagopuram built by Vijayanagara Emperor Krishnadevaraya in 1509 CE, and a sacred 3,500-year-old mango tree whose four branches yield four distinct types of fruit.

name: Kailasanathar Temple Kanchipuram
description: Constructed between 685 and 705 CE by Pallava King Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha), celebrated as the oldest surviving structural stone temple in Kanchipuram and the foundational prototype that inspired both the Shore Temple of Mamallapuram and the Kailash Temple at Ellora, built of soft sandstone featuring 58 miniature sub-shrines and dramatic rearing lion (yali) pillars.

name: Kamakshi Amman Temple Kanchipuram
description: Situated in the heart of Kanchipuram, one of the foremost 51 Shakti Peethas (Nabhi Kshetra) and the supreme Devi temple of South India, where Goddess Kamakshi is seated in the Padmasana yogic posture holding a sugarcane bow and lotus flowers, with the golden-plated Gayathri Mandapam housing the sacred Sri Chakra (Kamoti Peetha) consecrated by Adi Shankaracharya to channel divine benevolent energy.

name: Chitharal Jain Rock-Cut Monuments Kanyakumari
description: Perched atop a scenic rocky hillock in Chitharal village in Kanyakumari district, a major Digambar Jain monastic center established in the 9th century CE by Digambar monks, featuring natural granite overhangs adorned with masterfully carved rock-cut relief statues of Lord Parshvanatha, Mahavira, and Padmavathi Devi, later consecrated as the Bhagavathi Amman Temple in the 13th century.

name: Kanyakumari Bhagavathi Amman Temple & Triveni Sangam
description: Perched on the southern tip of the Indian subcontinent overlooking the Triveni Sangam where the Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea, and Indian Ocean merge, a celebrated 3,000-year-old coastal Shakti Peetha dedicated to Goddess Kanya Kumari (the virgin goddess), world-famous for her sparkling diamond nose ring whose brilliant reflection historically caused passing ships to mistake it for a lighthouse and shipwreck on rocks, prompting priests to keep the sea-facing eastern door permanently closed.

name: Mathoor Aqueduct (Mathoor Hanging Trough)
description: Constructed in 1966 across the deep valley of the Pahrali River near Thiruvattar in Kanyakumari district, recognized as one of the longest and highest water aqueducts in Asia, rising 115 feet (35 meters) above the lush green river canopy with a length of 1,240 feet (378 meters) supported by 28 colossal concrete pillars, carrying canal water between two mountain ridges.

name: Muttom Beach & 1875 Lighthouse Kanyakumari
description: Situated in Muttom village 16 km from Nagercoil on the Arabian Sea, an exceptionally picturesque coastal landscape famous for its towering red laterite sea cliffs dropping vertically into crashing waves, natural stone groynes, and a 100-foot-high historic lighthouse constructed by the British in 1875 offering sweeping aerial ocean panoramas.

name: Padmanabhapuram Palace Kanyakumari
description: Constructed around 1601 CE by Iravi Varma Kulasekhara Perumal and embellished by Maharaja Anizham Thirunal Marthanda Varma at the foot of the Veli Hills, celebrated as the largest wooden palace complex in Asia, built entirely in indigenous Kerala wood craftsmanship with rosewood ceilings, 90 varieties of floral carvings, Belgian mirrors, secret escape tunnels, and lustrous black oxide floors polished with egg-white and burnt coconut shells.

name: Sothavilai Beach Kanyakumari
description: Stretching for over 4 kilometers along the southern tip of India 10 km from Kanyakumari town, one of the longest and most pristine natural beaches in Tamil Nadu, characterized by powdery golden-white sand dunes, shallow gentle surf safe for swimming, swaying casuarina groves, and elevated sea-viewing gazebos.

name: Suchindram Thanumalayan Temple
description: Situated 11 km from Kanyakumari, an extraordinary 17th-century architectural marvel enshrining the Hindu Trinity in a single Lingam known as 'Thanumalayan' (Thanu-Shiva, Mal-Vishnu, Ayan-Brahma), celebrated for its 134-foot white entrance gopuram decorated with over 1,000 stucco figures, a colossal 22-foot monolithic statue of Lord Hanuman, and four musical granite pillars that resonate with musical notes.

name: Thiruvattar Adikesava Perumal Temple
description: Encircled on three sides by the holy Kothai and Pahrali rivers in Kanyakumari district, celebrated as the older prototype that inspired Thiruvananthapuram's Padmanabhaswamy Temple, enshrining a colossal 22-foot monolithic reclining idol of Lord Adikesava Perumal fashioned from 16,008 sacred Salagrama stones bound with Katusarkara herbal paste, viewed through three separate sanctum doors.

name: Udayagiri Fort & De Lannoy Tomb
description: Constructed in 1600 CE and reconstructed with massive granite blocks in 1742 by King Marthanda Varma of Travancore under the supervision of captured Dutch naval commander Eustachius De Lannoy, a sprawling 90-acre fortress nestled at the foot of an isolated hill, housing the historic tomb and chapel of General De Lannoy, a deer park, and a bio-diversity herbal garden.

name: Vattakottai Fort Kanyakumari
description: Built in the 18th century CE under Travancore King Marthanda Varma by Flemish naval commander Captain Eustachius De Lannoy, a scenic circular granite coastal fort occupying 3.5 acres on a rocky headland jutting directly into the Bay of Bengal, featuring 25-foot-high granite walls, cannon embrasures, and elevated battlements with spectacular ocean vistas.

name: Vivekananda Rock Memorial & Thiruvalluvar Statue
description: Standing on two distinct natural granite rock islands 500 meters off the southern tip of India where the Arabian Sea, Bay of Bengal, and Indian Ocean meet, comprising the 1970 Vivekananda Rock Memorial commemorating where Swami Vivekananda attained enlightenment in December 1892, and the neighboring colossal 133-foot (40.5 m) stone statue of ancient Tamil philosopher-poet Thiruvalluvar sculpted by V. Ganapati Sthapati using 7,000 tonnes of granite.

name: Vivekananda Rock Memorial Kanyakumari
description: Constructed in 1970 on a rocky island 500 meters off India's southernmost mainland tip where Swami Vivekananda meditated for three days in 1892, standing dramatically at the confluence of the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal, and the Indian Ocean.

name: Mayiladumparai Archaeological Site Krishnagiri
description: Situated amidst granite rock shelters and megalithic dolmens near Bargur in Krishnagiri district, an extraordinary archaeological site excavated by the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology, where AMS radiocarbon dating of iron artifacts yielded an unprecedented date of 2172 BCE, pushing back the origin of iron metallurgy in India and South Asia to over 4,200 years ago.

name: Arittapatti Biodiversity Heritage Site
description: Notified in November 2022 as the very first Biodiversity Heritage Site in Tamil Nadu, spanning 193 hectares across a chain of seven barren granite inselbergs in Melur taluka, harboring over 250 bird species (including rare raptors like Laggar Falcon and Shaheen Falcon), slender loris, 72 water bodies built during the 16th century, and a 2,200-year-old rock-cut Jain cave with Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions.

name: Gandhi Memorial Museum Madurai
description: Housed inside the historic 17th-century summer palace of Rani Mangammal of the Nayak dynasty in Madurai, established in 1959 as one of the five official National Gandhi Museums in India, consecrated at the very city where Mahatma Gandhi famously adopted the simple loincloth in 1921 to identify with the poor, displaying the original blood-stained garment worn by Gandhi when he was assassinated on 30 January 1948.

name: Goripalayam Dargah Madurai
description: Situated on the northern bank of the Vaigai River in Madurai, a colossal 13th-century Sufi shrine complex holding the holy tombs of two warrior-saints from Oman (Hazrat Sultan Alauddin Badusha and Hazrat Sultan Shamsuddin Badusha), famous for its monumental 70-foot-wide and 20-foot-high central dome carved entirely out of a single monolithic block of Azhaga Malai granite, and an ancient Tamil inscription by King Veerappa Nayak.

name: Kallalagar Temple Alagar Kovil
description: Nestled at the picturesque forested base of the Alagar Hills 21 km north of Madurai, an ancient Vaishnavite Divya Desam constructed by early Pandyas and Vijayanagara kings, enshrining Lord Vishnu as 'Sundararajar' (Kallalagar) holding golden weapons, surrounded by the ruins of an ancient earthen citadel, famous for the Chithirai Festival where Lord Alagar journeys on a golden horse to enter the Vaigai River.

name: Kazimar Big Mosque Madurai
description: Constructed in 1284 CE by Hazrat Kazi Syed Tajuddin (a direct descendant of Prophet Muhammad who arrived from Oman during the reign of Pandya King Kulasekara Pandyan), celebrated as the oldest Islamic monument and mosque in Madurai, accommodating over 2,500 worshippers under delicate plaster domes, housing the historic Madurai Maqbara dargah of the Madurai Hazrats and an ancient madrasa.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple Madurai
description: Situated on the southern bank of the Vaigai River in the 2,500-year-old city of Madurai, a colossal 14-acre Dravidian temple complex dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (Parvati) and Sundareswarar (Shiva), dominated by 14 monumental gopurams adorned with thousands of vibrant stucco figures.

name: Pazhamudircholai Murugan Temple
description: Nestled amidst dense evergreen deciduous forests in the scenic Alagar Hills 25 km from Madurai, the sixth and final abode (Arupadaiveedu) of Lord Murugan, where Lord Murugan is enshrined alongside both his consorts Valli and Deivanai, famous for the sacred perennial mountain spring 'Noopura Gangai' (Silambaru) and the legendary Blackberry tree (Naval Maram) associated with poetess Avvaiyar.

name: Samanar Malai (Jain Hill) Keelakuyilkudi
description: Rising dramatically above the agricultural plains in Keelakuyilkudi 15 km west of Madurai, a 2,000-year-old sacred granite hill where Digambar Jain monks lived, meditated, and attained Samadhi from the 2nd century BCE to the 10th century CE, featuring the Settipodavu and Pechipalle caves with sculpted Tirthankaras, Tamil-Brahmi and Vatteluttu inscriptions, and an ancient lotus pond.

name: Thirumalai Nayak Palace Madurai
description: Constructed in 1636 CE by King Thirumalai Nayak of the Madurai Nayak dynasty with the assistance of an Italian architect, an architectural masterpiece fusing classic Dravidian, Islamic, and European Renaissance styles, renowned for its colossal central courtyard (Swarga Vilasam) framed by massive fluted stone pillars soaring 82 feet high and 19 feet in circumference, with painted foliage stucco domes.

name: Thirupparankundram Murugan Temple
description: Carved into a massive monolithic granite hill on the southern outskirts of Madurai, the first and foremost of the sacred six abodes (Arupadaiveedu) of Lord Murugan, constructed in the 8th century CE under Pandya King Maravarman Sundara Pandyan, where Lord Murugan married Indra's daughter Deivanai in thanksgiving after vanquishing the asuras, featuring extraordinary rock-cut shrines to Shiva, Vishnu, Durga, and Ganesha.

name: Danish Fort Tharangambadi (Fort Dansborg)
description: Built in 1620 CE by Danish admiral Ove Gjedde on land leased from Thanjavur King Raghunatha Nayak in the sleepy coastal town of Tharangambadi ('Land of the Singing Waves'), recognized as the second largest Danish castle in the world after Kronborg Castle in Denmark, featuring trapezoidal sea-facing stone bastions, barrel-vaulted governor's quarters, and an archaeological museum displaying Danish trade relics.

name: Poompuhar
description: Tucked away in the southernmost tip of Thanjavur district, Poompuhar, also known as Puhar, is a quaint town that holds the remnants of a rich and storied past. Its name is inextricably linked to the legendary Tamil king, Nedunjeliyan, who ruled this land in the 2nd century BCE. The town's history is woven into its scenic landscape, where the tranquil waters of the Bay of Bengal meet the rugged Vellar estuary. Poompuhar is an ideal destination for trekkers, nature enthusiasts, and adventure-seekers, who come to explore its lush mangrove forests, mudflats, and pristine beaches, teeming with diverse marine life and an assortment of bird species.

name: Thirukadaiyur Amritaghateswarar Abhirami Temple
description: Constructed in the 10th century CE by Chola kings near the coast of Mayiladuthurai district, celebrated as the cosmic site where Lord Shiva emerged from the Lingam as Kalantaka (Destroyer of Death) to rescue his 16-year-old devotee Markandeya from Yama, and where poet Abhirami Bhattar made the new moon shine like full moon with his devotional hymns (Abhirami Antati), renowned as the foremost temple in India for Sashtiabdhapoorthi (60th) and Sadabhishekam (80th) renewal of marriage vows.

name: Tranquebar
description: Tranquebar, a quaint coastal town in Tamil Nadu, is a charming blend of Danish colonial heritage and Indian beach culture. Founded in 1620 by the Danish, this historic town boasts a unique architecture that reflects its rich cultural diversity. As you stroll through its narrow streets, you'll discover centuries-old churches, charming homes, and ancient ruins that whisper tales of the past. With its pristine beaches, tranquil backwaters, and vibrant cultural scene, Tranquebar is an idyllic getaway for those seeking a relaxing escape from the hustle and bustle of city life. Whether you're a history buff, a beach lover, or an adventure-seeker, Tranquebar has something for everyone.

name: Basilica of Our Lady of Good Health Velankanni
description: Situated on the shores of the Bay of Bengal 12 km south of Nagapattinam, celebrated across the Christian world as the 'Lourdes of the East', a monumental Roman Catholic Minor Basilica constructed in pure Gothic architectural style with soaring white spires and red-tiled roofs, commemorating three 16th-century apparitions of Mother Mary, drawing over 20 million pilgrims of all faiths annually.

name: Sikkal Singaravelar Temple
description: Located 5 km from Nagapattinam, an ancient temple celebrating the divine legend where Lord Murugan received his invincible weapon, the 'Shakti Vel', from his mother Goddess Velnedunkanni to vanquish the demon king Surapadman, famous during the annual Soorasamharam festival for the miraculous phenomenon of the bronze idol sweating real perspiration after receiving the spear.

name: Kolli Hills
description: Tucked away in the Panniyar Range of the Eastern Ghats, the Kolli Hills stand as an untouched paradise in Tamil Nadu. The hills' misty climate, rolling hills, and verdant forests have captivated travelers for centuries. The area is home to various species of birds, butterflies, and even rare orchids, creating an enchanting atmosphere for those seeking a tranquil getaway. From leisurely treks to photography expeditions, Kolli Hills offers a diverse experience for adventure-seekers and nature enthusiasts alike.

name: Namakkal Fort & Narasimha Cave Temple
description: Perched dramatically atop a 246-foot-high sheer single granite rock monolith occupying 1.5 acres in the center of Namakkal town, constructed in the 16th century by Ramachandra Nayak and fortified by Hyder Ali, housing an ancient stepwell, cannon bastions, and flanking two extraordinary 8th-century Adiyaman rock-cut cave temples dedicated to Lord Narasimha and Ranganatha.

name: Archedin Hills View Point Echo
description: A secluded mountain crest in the southern Nilgiris overlooking steep amphitheater valleys, famous for striking echo reverberations across the tea slopes.

name: Burliyar Bridge
description: Historic mountain road and railway bridge spanning the Burliyar torrent on the Mettupalayam-Coonoor ghat road, adjoining the historic 1871 Burliyar State Horticultural Farm.

name: Catherine Falls Kotagiri
description: Located near Kotagiri in the Nilgiri Hills, a breathtaking 250-foot (76 m) double-cascading waterfall formed by the Kallar River crashing through a dramatic deep mountain gorge, surrounded by emerald green tea plantations, shola forests, and named in memory of Catherine, the wife of pioneer coffee planter M. D. Cockburn.

name: Coonoor Black Bridge
description: Historic bridge crossing the stream in Wellington Cantonment, originally built of black-tarred Burmese teak wood in 1858 connecting the barracks to the officers' mess.

name: Coonoor Law's Falls
description: Named after Colonel Law who built the Coonoor Ghat Road, a cascading waterfall tumbling down rocky boulders along the Coonoor-Mettupalayam highway.

name: Coonoor Madras Regiment Museum
description: Located at the Madras Regimental Centre (MRC) in Wellington Cantonment, showcasing the battle history, arms, uniforms, and war memorabilia of the Indian Army's oldest infantry regiment (raised 1758).

name: Coonoor Manekshaw Bridge
description: The modernized bridge across the Wellington stream rechristened Manekshaw Bridge in memory of Field Marshal Sam Manekshaw, who chose to spend his retired life in Wellington.

name: Coonoor Nilgiri Mountain Railway Bridge
description: An iconic stone arch railway viaduct spanning a mountain ravine, where the UNESCO-listed toy train chugs over deep valleys surrounded by tea plantations.

name: Coonoor Nilgiris Tea Garden
description: Vast rolling carpets of fragrant high-grown Nilgiri tea bushes covering the hillsides of Coonoor at 6,000 feet, producing aromatic, brisk golden teas.

name: Coonoor Sim's Park
description: Developed in 1874 by J.D. Sim, a 12-hectare botanical garden terraced into a natural ravine, showcasing over 1,000 species of temperate flora including rare Rudraksha and Queensland Karry Pine trees.

name: Coonoor Sim's Park Hidden Valley Fountain
description: A tranquil natural spring fountain tucked in the deep lower ravine valley of Sim's Park, shaded by ancient tree ferns and towering Tasmanian blue gums.

name: Coonoor Wellington Gymkhana Club
description: Established in 1873 in the British cantonment of Wellington, a colonial country club featuring an 18-hole championship golf course surrounded by soaring cypress trees and tea slopes.

name: Coonoor Wellington Lake
description: A tranquil, immaculately maintained freshwater lake nestled amidst pine woods and manicured turf in Wellington Cantonment, featuring shaded walking paths and resting benches.

name: Doddabetta Peak Ooty
description: Rising to an altitude of 2,637 meters (8,652 feet) just 9 km from Ooty, the highest mountain summit in the Nilgiri Hills and the fourth highest peak in South India, situated at the junction of the Western and Eastern Ghats, featuring a TTDC Telescope House with two high-powered telescopes providing 360-degree aerial panoramas of the Blue Mountains.

name: Dolphin's Nose View Point Coonoor
description: An enormous protruding rock promontory shaped like a dolphin's nose, rising 1,550 meters above sea level, providing vistas of Catherine Falls plunging into the canyon below.

name: Emerald Lake & Avalanche Lake Nilgiris
description: Nestled 22 km south of Ooty in the Silent Valley region of the Nilgiris, a pair of pristine, crystal-clear high-altitude lakes surrounded by rolling emerald green tea estates, dense shola woodlands, and blooming wild rhododendrons, famous for rainbow trout fishing, pine camping, and eco-safaris into the Upper Bhavani sanctuary.

name: Government Botanical Garden Ooty
description: Laid out in 1848 by William Graham McIvor across 55 terraced acres on the lower slopes of Doddabetta Peak in Ooty, one of the oldest and most celebrated botanical gardens in India, featuring over 1,000 species of exotic and indigenous plants, six distinct sections including an Italian Garden, Fern House, Japanese Garden, and a 20-million-year-old fossilized tree trunk presented by the Geological Survey of India.

name: Government Rose Garden Ooty
description: Situated on the slopes of Elk Hill at an altitude of 7,200 feet in Ooty, established in 1995 to commemorate the centenary of the Ooty Flower Show, recognized as the largest rose garden in India, laid out across 10 terraced acres featuring over 20,000 rose bushes spanning 2,800 varieties, including miniature roses, ramblers, hybrid tea roses, green roses, and black roses, honored with the Garden of Excellence Award by the World Federation of Rose Societies.

name: Hillgrove Scenic Train Pass
description: A vintage mountain railway station on the UNESCO World Heritage Nilgiri Mountain Railway (NMR), where steam locomotives halt to refill water from mountain springs amidst lush coffee estates.

name: Huligal Hills Coonoor
description: A quaint panchayat village and mountain ridge perched high above the Coonoor valley, famous for smallholder orthodox tea gardens and breathtaking drop-off viewpoints.

name: Kodanad Viewpoint Kotagiri
description: Perched at the eastern tip of the Nilgiris ridge 18 km from Kotagiri, one of the most spectacular natural viewpoints in southern India, offering breathtaking 240-degree panoramic vistas where the Blue Mountains drop precipitously into the deep Moyar River gorge, overlooking Bhavanisagar Dam, the Mysore plateau, and Rangaswamy Peak.

name: Kolakambai Waterfalls (Kullakamby)
description: Dropping roughly 400 feet into a rugged canyon in the southern Nilgiri ranges, Kolakambai Falls is one of the highest unbroken waterfalls in Tamil Nadu.

name: Kotagiri
description: The last preserved urban natural pocket of pristine shola rainforest with quiet birding paths.

name: Masinagudi Maravakandy Dam
description: Constructed in 1951 in the foothills of the Nilgiris near Masinagudi in Mudumalai Tiger Reserve, this reservoir acts as a vital watering hole for wild elephant herds, tigers, and dholes.

name: Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (Theppakadu Elephant Camp)
description: Spanning 321 square kilometers on the northwestern slope of the Nilgiris contiguous with Bandipur and Wayanad, declared a Tiger Reserve in 2007, famous for hosting over 100 Royal Bengal tigers, leopards, Asian elephants, and the historic Theppakadu Elephant Camp established in 1910 on the Moyar River, immortalized in the Oscar-winning documentary 'The Elephant Whisperers'.

name: Mukurthi National Park Nilgiris
description: Covering 78 square kilometers of montane grasslands and high-altitude Shola valleys in the western corner of the Nilgiris plateau at an average elevation of 7,800 feet, established as a National Park in 1990 as a strict wilderness sanctuary to protect the endangered endemic Nilgiri Tahr, featuring pristine rolling downs, Mukurthi Peak (2,554 m), and the sparkling Mukurthi Lake.

name: Ooty Arboretum & Tea Garden
description: Established near Ooty Lake across 1.5 hectares, dedicated exclusively to conserving indigenous Western Ghats shola trees and highland flora, bordered by gentle tea slopes.

name: Ooty Commercial Street
description: The bustling main retail spine of Ooty, lined with heritage bakeries, artisanal handmade chocolate shops, woolen knitwear outlets, and leather craft boutiques.

name: Ooty CSI St. Stephen's Church
description: Consecrated in 1830, one of the oldest churches in the Nilgiris, built with massive teak timber salvaged from Tipu Sultan's Lal Bagh palace at Srirangapatna, hauled up the mountains by elephants.

name: Ooty Government Botanical Garden (Horticulture)
description: Laid out in 1848 by William Graham McIvor on the lower slopes of Doddabetta Peak, sprawling over 55 terraced acres with thousands of indigenous and exotic plants, glasshouses, and a 20-million-year-old fossilized tree trunk.

name: Ooty Government Museum
description: Established in 1989 on Mysore Road, showcasing the rich ethnographic history of the indigenous Nilgiri tribes (Toda, Kota, Kurumba, Irula, and Paniyan), their traditional dwellings, tools, and handicrafts.

name: Ooty Ketti Valley Viewpoint
description: Widely cited as the second largest inhabited gorge valley in the world, stretching over 14 kilometers down towards Mettupalayam, dotted with colorful Badaga villages and vegetable terraces.

name: Ooty Lake Boating
description: Constructed in 1824 by John Sullivan, the founder of British Ooty, an expansive 65-acre lake surrounded by towering eucalyptus groves, featuring rowing, pedal, and motor boats.

name: Ooty Municipal Market
description: A bustling 150-year-old covered central bazaar featuring over 1,500 stalls selling crisp English vegetables (carrots, baby potatoes, beets, cabbage), Toda embroidery, and mountain spices.

name: Ooty Pine Forest
description: A majestic hillside forest of soaring Siberian pine trees planted in the early 20th century, sloping gently down towards the tranquil waters of Kamaraj Sagar Dam (Sandynallah Reservoir).

name: Ooty Railway Hill Station
description: The terminus of the 1908 Nilgiri Mountain Railway (UNESCO World Heritage Site), celebrated for its charming Victorian gabled architecture, vintage clock tower, and operational steam engine sheds.

name: Ooty Romantic Boating (Honeymoon Boat House)
description: Located at the tranquil western shore of Ooty Lake (Honeymoon Boat House), offering couples private customized shikara-style covered boat rides across secluded inlets.

name: Ooty Thunder World Amusement Park
description: Also known as Dinosaur Park, a themed indoor/outdoor entertainment park in Ooty featuring animatronic prehistoric dinosaurs, 5D cinema, haunted house, and vortex tunnel.

name: Ooty Tiger Point
description: A dramatic cliff-edge viewpoint along the upper ridges of Ooty, historically associated with tiger movements between the Bhavani and Moyar river valleys.

name: Ooty Upper Bazaar
description: The authentic traditional market area perched on the upper ridge of Ooty, known for wholesale hill garlic, Nilgiri spices, tea merchants, and historic local eateries.

name: Pakasuran Peak View Point Coonoor (Droog Fort)
description: Historically known as Bakthasuran Kottai or Droog Fort, a 16th-century military outpost used by Tipu Sultan, perched precariously on a 6,000-foot cliff edge reachable via a 3-km tea trail trek.

name: Pykara Waterfalls & Pykara Lake Ooty
description: Flowing through the Mukurthi National Park buffer 21 km from Ooty, the Pykara River is considered deeply sacred by the indigenous Toda tribe, celebrated for its twin stepped waterfalls plunging 55 meters and 61 meters over smooth granite rocks amidst rolling pine downs, alongside Pykara Lake featuring an MTDC boathouse with speedboats and cafeterias.

name: Sim's Park Coonoor
description: Developed in 1874 by J. D. Sim and Major Murray in a natural ravine at an elevation of 5,800 feet in Coonoor, a world-class 30-acre botanical garden landscaped in traditional Japanese style, home to over 1,000 species of rare exotic and temperate plants, including Queensland Karry pines, cinnamon, camphor, rudraksha trees, and an annual fruit and vegetable show in May.

name: Sleeping Lady View Point
description: A scenic vantage point overlooking the Nilgiri mountain horizon whose natural ridge contours form the unmistakable silhouette of a reclining lady sleeping peacefully against the sky.

name: St. Stephen's Church Ooty
description: Constructed in 1829 CE under Governor Stephen Rumbold Lushington on Club Road in Ooty, the oldest church in the Nilgiris, celebrated for its unique historical architectural materials featuring massive teakwood timber beams hauled by elephants up the ghats from the dismantled Lal Bagh Palace of Tipu Sultan at Srirangapatna, accompanied by exquisite stained-glass windows and a historic cemetery holding John Sullivan's grave.

name: Tea Museum & Tea Factory Ooty
description: Perched amidst rolling emerald tea slopes at an altitude of 6,000 feet on Doddabetta Road in Ooty, a state-of-the-art interactive tea museum and live operational processing factory, displaying the global history of tea from ancient China to the Nilgiris, walking visitors through live CTC leaf withering, crushing, fermenting, drying, and tasting of freshly brewed cardamom and ginger teas.

name: Avudaiyarkoil (Thiruperunturai)
description: Constructed in the 9th century CE by prime minister and Saivite saint-poet Manikkavacakar with royal gold entrusted to him to buy Arabian cavalry horses, an architecturally sublime temple dedicated to Lord Athmanathar (Shiva), unique across India because the inner sanctum contains neither an idol nor a stone Lingam, worshipping the Supreme as formless space (Nirakara) symbolized by a brass bowl (deeparadhana plate).

name: Kodumbalur Moovar Koil Pudukkottai
description: Constructed in the 10th century CE by Chola general and Irukkuvel chieftain Boothi Vikramakesari in Kodumbalur, an architectural masterpiece of early Dravidian stone temple craftsmanship originally comprising three identical stone temples (Moovar Koil) of which two survive today in breathtaking pristine detail, renowned for their intricate miniature bas-reliefs, Ardhanariswara sculptures, and Kalari Shiva dance postures.

name: Kudumiyanmalai Sikhagiriswarar Temple & Inscriptions
description: Situated at the foot of a granite hill in Pudukkottai, an ancient rock-cut temple complex dedicated to Lord Sikhagiriswarar, celebrated globally among musicologists for its monumental 7th-century 38-line rock-cut musical inscription engraved under Pallava King Mahendravarman I, detailing the seven classical Indian musical notes (swaras) across seven ancient ragas.

name: Narthamalai Vijayalaya Choleeswaram & Caves
description: Perched on Melamalai hill in Narthamalai, an extraordinary architectural marvel constructed in the 9th century CE by Muttaraiyar chieftains and renovated by Vijayalaya Chola (founder of the Imperial Chola dynasty), celebrated for its rare circular inner sanctum enclosed within a square vimana, flanked by two 8th-century rock-cut cave temples and ancient water reservoirs.

name: Sittannavasal Cave & 9th-Century Jain Frescoes
description: Perched on a prominent granite hill in Pudukkottai district, an internationally celebrated rock-cut Jain monastic cave complex featuring the 7th-century Arivar Koil cave temple adorned with masterwork vegetable-dye fresco paintings of dancing apsaras and monks gathering lotus flowers in a pond, and 'Eladipattam' (17 polished stone beds with 2nd-century BCE Asokan Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions).

name: Tirumayam Fort & Rock-Cut Cave Temples
description: Constructed in 1687 CE by Sethupathi Vijaya Raghunatha Thevar of Ramanathapuram atop a massive granite hill spanning 40 acres, an extraordinary concentric ring fortress with three layers of defensive stone walls, royal cannons, and rock-cut cave temples beneath the fort dedicated to Satyagiriswarar (Shiva) and Sathyamurthi Perumal (reclining Vishnu), holding rare 8th-century Pandya bas-reliefs.

name: Viralimalai Murugan Temple & Peacock Sanctuary
description: Perched on an isolated granite hillock 30 km from Trichy, an ancient 15th-century temple dedicated to Lord Murugan (Shanmuganathar) enshrined with six faces and twelve arms seated on a peacock alongside Valli and Deivayanai, reached by climbing 207 stone steps through a natural deciduous scrub forest designated as a natural peacock sanctuary sheltering hundreds of wild Indian peafowl.

name: Ariyaman Beach (Kushi Beach) Ramanathapuram
description: Situated on the Palk Bay along the Madurai-Rameswaram highway near Mandapam, an exceptionally wide and tranquil 150-meter-broad sandy beach stretching for 2 kilometers, renowned for its crystal-clear non-turbulent waters completely free of high waves, shaded by thick casuarina groves, equipped by Tamil Nadu Tourism with water scooters, parasailing, and boat houses.

name: Devipattinam Navagrahapasanasthal (Navabashanam Sea Temple)
description: Located on the shallow shores of the Palk Strait 15 km from Ramanathapuram, an ancient coastal pilgrimage site celebrated in Hindu mythology where Lord Rama installed nine stone pillars representing the Navagrahas (nine planetary deities) directly into the sea bed to seek blessings before marching his army to Lanka, which remain partially submerged in gentle sea waves.

name: Dhanushkodi Ghost Town & Beach
description: Situated at the eastern tip of Pamban Island just 24 kilometers from Talaimannar in Sri Lanka, a haunting ghost town destroyed by the devastating 1964 Rameswaram cyclone, featuring atmospheric ruins of a colonial railway station, church, and hospital beside windswept sand dunes.

name: Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam National Memorial Rameswaram
description: Constructed in 2017 by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) over the resting place of India's 11th President and beloved 'Missile Man' Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam in Peikarumbu on Rameswaram Island, blending Mughal, Indian temple, and Chettinad architectural elements, displaying life-size statues, hundreds of personal artifacts, and scale models of Agni and Prithvi missiles.

name: Kothandaramaswamy Temple Dhanushkodi
description: Perched on a narrow strip of sand 12 km from Rameswaram, surrounded on all sides by the shimmering turquoise waters of the Gulf of Mannar and Palk Strait, a sacred 500-year-old temple where Vibhishana (brother of Ravana) surrendered to Lord Rama and was crowned King of Lanka, famous across India as the only historical structure that miraculously survived completely intact during the catastrophic 1964 Dhanushkodi cyclone.

name: Kurusadai Island
description: Located in the Gulf of Mannar, off the coast of Tamil Nadu, Kurusadai Island is a serene getaway that promises to leave you enchanted. This small, picturesque island is a part of the Pamban Islands group and is surrounded by crystal-clear waters teeming with marine life. The island's pristine beaches, mangrove forests, and coral reefs make it an ideal destination for snorkeling, swimming, and sunbathing. The island's unique topography and biodiversity create a fascinating environment where you can spot a variety of birds, including ospreys, and engage in exciting activities like boat rides and beach walks. Kurusadai Island is a true gem of Tamil Nadu, waiting to be explored and cherished.

name: Pamban Bridge (Cantilever Sea Bridge)
description: Opened on 24 February 1914 across the treacherous waters of the Palk Strait, India's very first sea bridge spanning 2.06 kilometers (1.28 miles) on 143 concrete piers, connecting the mainland town of Mandapam to Rameswaram Island, celebrated for its double-leaf bascule Scherzer rolling lift span that opens manually to allow ships and naval vessels to pass underneath.

name: Ramalinga Vilasam Palace Ramanathapuram
description: Constructed between 1674 and 1710 CE by Kizhavan Sethupathi (Raghunatha Kilavan), the legendary royal palace of the Sethupathi rulers of Ramnad, celebrated across India for its extraordinary wall-to-ceiling fresco murals depicting 18th-century battles with the Dutch East India Company and Arcot Nawabs, royal durbars, hunting scenes, and Ramayana legends.

name: Ramanathaswamy Temple Rameswaram
description: One of the twelve sacred Shiva Jyotirlingas and one of the four holy Char Dhams, located on Pamban Island where Lord Rama worshipped Shiva after vanquishing Ravana, renowned for having the longest pillared corridor in the world (over 1,200 meters).

name: Mettur Dam (Stanley Reservoir)
description: Constructed between 1925 and 1934 across the sacred Cauvery River where it enters the plains, one of the oldest and largest masonry gravity dams in India rising 214 feet with a crest length of 5,600 feet, creating the vast 60-mile-long Stanley Reservoir with an active capacity of 93 billion cubic feet, featuring the scenic hillside Ellis Park and illuminated fountains.

name: Sankagiri Fort Salem
description: Rising dramatically 1,000 feet above the surrounding plains in Salem district, a colossal 14-tiered hill fortress constructed in the 15th century by Vijayanagara rulers and later heavily fortified by Hyder Ali, Tipu Sultan, and the British, featuring 14 defensive gate walls, rock-cut water tanks, a cliff-hanging granary, and immortalized as the site where Kongu freedom fighter Dheeran Chinnamalai was hanged by the British in 1805.

name: Yercaud Lake & Emerald Park
description: Known as the 'Jewel of the South' at 4,970 feet in the Shevaroy Hills of the Eastern Ghats, centered around the picturesque Emerald Lake surrounded by cool deodar groves, coffee plantations, and the manicured Anna Park.

name: Athangudi Palace & Heritage Tile Workshops
description: Situated in the heritage village of Athangudi 12 km from Karaikudi, famous for its magnificent 19th-century Chettinad merchant palace featuring opulent Belgian mirrors, hand-carved teakwood ceilings, and world-renowned for the artisanal Athangudi Tiles (GI tagged), which are handcrafted individually using local river sand, cement, and colored pigments poured into brass stencils.

name: Chettinad
description: Tucked away in the Sivaganga district of Tamil Nadu, Chettinad is a trekker's paradise. This lesser-explored region is a tapestry of rugged terrain, meandering rivers, and ancient temple ruins. Trek through the dense forests, climb limestone cliffs, and spot exotic birds in their natural habitat. The terrain here is as rugged as it is rewarding, with each step leading to a new discovery. With its pristine waterfalls, rolling hills, and scenic vistas, Chettinad beckons the adventurer within. Take a journey off the beaten path and immerse yourself in the unspoiled beauty of Chettinad.

name: Keezhadi Archaeological Site & World-Class Sangam Museum
description: Situated 12 km southeast of Madurai on the ancient banks of the Vaigai River, an epoch-making archaeological excavation that proved second urbanization in South India contemporary with the Gangetic plains dating back to 580 BCE, featuring deep trenches revealing brick structures, closed ring-well drainage, weaving tools, carnelian beads, and a state-of-the-art heritage museum displaying over 6,000 Sangam-era artifacts.

name: Pillayarpatti Karpaga Vinayagar Temple
description: Carved into a granite hillock in Pillayarpatti 12 km from Karaikudi, celebrated as one of the oldest rock-cut cave temples in Tamil Nadu dating to the 4th-5th century CE under early Pandya rulers, enshrining a magnificent 6-foot monolithic rock-cut idol of Lord Karpaga Vinayagar (Ganesha) with two arms and his trunk curled uniquely to the right (Valampuri), facing northern celestial directions.

name: Courtallam
description: Situated in the Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu, Courtallam beckons nature enthusiasts with its 10 breathtaking waterfalls. This stunning mountain getaway offers a medley of thrilling waterfalls, lush green surroundings, and vibrant wildlife. Visitors can trek through the serene forests, take in the enchanting vistas, or simply relax at the base of these captivating waterfalls. The unique blend of Tamil Nadu's rich cultural heritage and Courtallam's majestic natural beauty creates an unforgettable experience.

name: Sankaranarayanan Temple Sankarankovil
description: Constructed in the 11th century CE by Pandya King Ukkira Pandyan in Tenkasi district, an ancient temple celebrating the unity of Shaivism and Vaishnavism by enshrining the unique combined deity 'Sankaranarayanan' (right half Lord Shiva with crescent moon and tiger skin, left half Lord Vishnu with conch and golden silk), famous for Goddess Gomathi Amman and the healing clay of its sacred tank.

name: Adi Kumbeswarar Temple Kumbakonam
description: Constructed in the 7th century CE by Chola kings and expanded by the Vijayanagara rulers across 4 acres, the primary Shaivite temple from which the town of Kumbakonam derives its name, where Lord Shiva is worshipped as a Lingam formed from the divine pot (Kumbha) of nectar broken by Shiva's arrow after the cosmic deluge, famous as the religious epicentre of the 12-year Mahamaham festival.

name: Airavatesvara Temple Darasuram
description: Constructed in the 12th century CE by Chola Emperor Rajaraja Chola II, the third of the UNESCO Great Living Chola Temples, celebrated worldwide for its museum-grade architectural finesse featuring a pillared mandapa carved into a monumental stone chariot drawn by galloping horses, singing musical steps (swara-padi) that produce melodic tones, and 73 relief panels illustrating Periya Puranam Shaiva saints.

name: Brihadeeswarar Temple Thanjavur (Big Temple)
description: Commissioned in 1010 CE by Emperor Raja Raja Chola I, an UNESCO World Heritage Site recognized as the 'Great Living Chola Temple', featuring an astonishing 216-foot granite vimana tower crowned by an 80-ton single monolithic granite dome (Kumbam).

name: Manora Fort Pattukkottai
description: Constructed in 1814 CE by Maratha King Serfoji II of Thanjavur on the shores of the Palk Strait near Pattukkottai, a unique eight-storeyed hexagonal stone victory minaret and fortress tower rising 75 feet, erected to commemorate the British victory over Napoleon Bonaparte at the Battle of Waterloo, encircled by a moat and defensive ramparts.

name: Sarangapani Temple Kumbakonam
description: Constructed by Nayak and Chola rulers in the temple city of Kumbakonam, one of the foremost of the 108 Vaishnavite Divya Desams, celebrated for its soaring 12-tiered 146-foot (45 m) Rajagopuram (the tallest in Kumbakonam), and a magnificent sanctum sculpted in the form of a celestial stone chariot drawn by elephants and horses with carved wheels and radiating spokes.

name: Suryanar Kovil (Navagraha Sun Temple)
description: Constructed during the reign of Chola Emperor Kulottunga Chola I (1075-1120 CE), the foremost and only temple in Tamil Nadu dedicated exclusively to the Sun God (Surya Bhagavan), where Surya is enshrined with his consorts Usha and Chhaya, surrounded by separate sanctums for all other eight planetary deities (Navagrahas) arranged in an astrological cosmic mandala.

name: Swamimalai Murugan Temple
description: Built on an artificial 60-foot-high hillock in Swamimalai near Kumbakonam, the fourth of the sacred six abodes (Arupadaiveedu) of Lord Murugan, celebrated as 'Swaminatha Swamy' who as a child preached the profound cosmic meaning of the Pranava Mantra ('Om') to his own father Lord Shiva, reached by climbing 60 stone steps representing the 60 Tamil years of the Hindu calendar cycle.

name: Thanjavur Maratha Royal Palace & Saraswathi Mahal Library
description: Constructed in 1535 CE by the Thanjavur Nayaks and expanded by the Bhonsle Maratha rulers, a colossal royal palace complex featuring the 190-foot seven-storeyed Goodagopuram observation tower, the Bell Tower, the royal Durbar Hall with gilded stucco ceilings, and the world-renowned Saraswathi Mahal Library founded in the 16th century holding over 60,000 rare palm-leaf and paper manuscripts.

name: Thirunageswaram Naganathar Temple (Rahu Stalam)
description: Constructed by Chola King Gandaraditya in the 10th century CE, celebrated as the premier Navagraha pilgrimage destination for planet Rahu (the shadow planet), where Lord Rahu is enshrined with human face and two consorts Nagavalli and Nagakanni, famous worldwide for the physical phenomenon where white cow's milk poured during abhishekam miraculously turns light blue upon touching the idol.

name: Kolukkumalai Tea Estate (World's Highest Tea Plantation)
description: Perched at an astonishing elevation of 7,900 feet (2,400 meters) on the rugged crest of the Western Ghats in Theni district, recognized globally as the highest tea plantation in the world, founded in the 1920s by British planters, producing rare orthodox mountain teas in a century-old heritage wooden tea factory, famous worldwide for surreal sunrise views above an endless ocean of rolling white clouds.

name: Kumbakarai Falls Theni
description: Situated at the foot of the Kodaikanal hills near Periyakulam, an exceptionally scenic two-tiered freshwater waterfall formed by the Pambar River as it trickles down the Palani slopes, where water collects in an upper rock pool and plunges 87 feet down over polished volcanic granite boulders into safe natural bathing lagoons.
