name: Meghamalai
description: Cloud-draped cardamom and organic tea estates surrounded by virgin shola forests and deep reservoir lakes.

name: Suruli Falls Theni
description: Nestled in the lush Meghamalai mountain slopes 56 km from Theni, an enchanting 150-foot two-stage perennial waterfall fed by the Suruli River, immortalized in the 5th-century CE Tamil epic Silappadikaram by Ilango Adigal, falling into a natural pool surrounded by 18 ancient rock-cut caves of the Kailasanathar temple.

name: Vaigai Dam Andipatti Theni
description: Built in 1959 across the sacred Vaigai River near Andipatti, an imposing 111-foot-high concrete and masonry dam that creates a vast freshwater reservoir supplying drinking water and irrigation to Madurai and Dindigul districts, featuring extensive manicured Mughal gardens modelled on Mysore's Brindavan Gardens with illuminated dancing fountains.

name: Adichanallur Archaeological Iron Age Site & On-Site Museum
description: Located on the banks of the sacred Thamirabarani River near Srivaikuntam, celebrated as one of the oldest and most extensive prehistoric megalithic burial grounds in India dating between 1000 BCE and 600 BCE, featuring thousands of giant clay burial urns (mudhumakkal thazhi) holding human skeletons, bronze animal figurines, iron swords, and India's first on-site archaeological museum.

name: Kalugumalai Rock-Cut Jain Monuments & Vettuvan Koil
description: Perched on a monumental rocky ridge in Thoothukudi district, celebrated by art historians as the 'Ellora of the South', featuring the unfinished 8th-century Vettuvan Koil (literally 'Sculptor's Paradise') carved top-down directly out of living granite rock by Pandya craftsmen, alongside a dramatic cliff face bearing over 150 finely sculpted Digambar Jain Tirthankara bas-reliefs and Vatteluttu inscriptions.

name: Korkai Ancient Pandyan Port & Archaeological Site
description: Situated near the mouth of the Thamirabarani River in Thoothukudi district, the legendary ancient port capital of the Early Pandyas mentioned in the 1st-century CE Greek treatise 'Periplus of the Erythraean Sea' and Ptolemy's Geography as 'Colchi', celebrated for 2,800 years of deep-sea pearl diving, featuring excavated brick platforms, ancient pottery kilns, and a sacred 2,000-year-old Vanni tree.

name: Kulasekarapattinam Kadaswamy Beach & Mutharamman Temple
description: Situated on the Gulf of Mannar coast in Thoothukudi district, an ancient port town founded by King Maravarman Kulasekaran, world-famous for its 300-year-old coastal Mutharamman Temple and the annual 10-day Dasara festival where over 1.5 million devotees undergo 41 days of fasting and dress up as deities, kings, beggars, and mythical beings before bathing in the sea on Vijayadashami.

name: Manapad Beach & Holy Cross Church
description: Perched on a high coastal sand dune promontory jutting into the Gulf of Mannar 18 km south of Tiruchendur, world-famous among international wave surfers for its naturally occurring point break, crowned by the historic 1540 CE Holy Cross Church holding a fragment of the True Cross of Jerusalem brought by St. Francis Xavier who lived and meditated in a natural sea cave here.

name: Our Lady of Snows Basilica Thoothukudi
description: Constructed in 1582 CE by Portuguese missionaries on the maritime coastline of Thoothukudi, an imposing Catholic Minor Basilica enshrining the miraculous wooden statue of Our Lady of Snows brought from Manila aboard the vessel Santa Helena in 1555 CE, celebrated for its French-inspired facade, gold-plated altar, and the colossal Golden Car festival attracting half a million coastal Paravar devotees.

name: Panchalankurichi Kattabomman Memorial Fort
description: Located in Panchalankurichi near Ottapidaram, the reconstructed historical fortress of legendary 18th-century Palaiyakkarar chieftain Veerapandiya Kattabomman, who waged fierce armed resistance against the British East India Company's taxation before being executed at Kayathar in October 1799, featuring high brick ramparts, an archaeological excavation gallery of the original fort, and the Sri Jakkamma Temple.

name: Sivagalai Archaeological Site Thoothukudi
description: Situated on a high gravel mound overlooking the Thamirabarani River basin in Thoothukudi district, an internationally recognized Iron Age burial site excavated by the Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology, where carbon accelerator mass spectrometry (AMS) dating of paddy husks inside burial urns yielded a scientific date of 1155 BCE, scientifically proving advanced rice cultivation in Tamil Nadu over 3,100 years ago.

name: Vallanadu Blackbuck Sanctuary Thoothukudi
description: Covering 1,641 acres of dry deciduous thorn and scrub forest across an isolated rocky hillock in Thoothukudi district, established in 1987 specifically to conserve the southernmost natural breeding population of the Indian Blackbuck (Antilope cervicapra) on the Asian continent, also sheltering spotted deer, jungle cats, monitor lizards, and over 100 bird species.

name: Jambukeswarar Temple Thiruvanaikaval
description: Constructed over 1,800 years ago by early Chola King Kocengannan on the Srirangam island, one of the five cosmic Pancha Bhoota Sthalams representing the element of Water (Appu Lingam), where the sacred Shiva Lingam remains perpetually submerged in clear natural spring water that flows from a subterranean natural aquifer.

name: Our Lady of Lourdes Church Trichy
description: Constructed in 1840 inside the St. Joseph's College campus near Rockfort in Tiruchirappalli, an imposing 200-foot-high Neo-Gothic architectural landmark modelled faithfully on the world-famous Basilica of Our Lady of Lourdes in southern France, featuring soaring ribbed vaulted arches, stained-glass clerestory windows depicting biblical narratives, and an iconic bell tower.

name: Sri Ranganathaswamy Temple Srirangam
description: Occupying a colossal 156 acres (63 hectares) on an island formed by the Cauvery and Kollidam rivers, recognized as the largest functioning Hindu temple complex in the world and the foremost of the 108 Vaishnavite Divya Desams, enclosed within 7 concentric rectangular prakaras with 21 magnificent gopurams, crowned by the soaring 73-meter-high (239 ft) Rajagopuram.

name: Ucchi Pillayar Temple Rockfort Trichy
description: Perched dramatically atop an 83-meter-high (273 ft) prehistoric volcanic rock that geologists estimate is 3.8 billion years old (older than the Himalayas), a 7th-century Pallava and Nayak rock-cut temple dedicated to Lord Ganesha, reached by climbing 437 stone-hewn steps through cool rock caverns and pillared mandapas.

name: Kalakad-Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve (KMTR)
description: Notified in 1988 across 895 square kilometers in the southern Western Ghats as Tamil Nadu's very first Tiger Reserve, recognized by UNESCO as one of the world's premier biodiversity hotspots, functioning as the vital watershed catchment for 14 major rivers including the sacred perennial Thamirabarani, sheltering Royal Bengal tigers, leopards, king cobras, and Nilgiri martens.

name: Koonthankulam Bird Sanctuary Tirunelveli
description: Spanning 129 hectares around Koonthankulam and Kadankulam village tanks in Nanguneri taluka, designated as an international Ramsar Wetland site in 2022, world-famous as an inspiring model of community-based bird conservation where over 100,000 migratory birds (including Bar-headed Geese, Greater Flamingos, and Painted Storks) breed directly in neem trees inside the village courtyards, strictly protected by local residents who ban firecrackers.

name: Manimuthar Falls
description: Manimuthar Falls is a natural waterfall located in the Tirunelveli district of Tamil Nadu. Situated inside the protected Kalakkad Mundanthurai Tiger Reserve, this waterfall is formed by the Manimuthar River cascading down a rocky face. The falls form a deep, natural pool at the bottom that is popular for swimming. Surrounded by hills and forests, it offers a refreshing, nature-rich escape.

name: Nellaiappar Temple Tirunelveli
description: Spread across 14 acres on the banks of the Thamirabarani River, an ancient Pandyan temple dedicated to Lord Shiva (Nellaiappar) and Goddess Gandhimathi, renowned for the Tamra Sabha (copper dance hall) and intricate musical pillars that produce musical notes when tapped.

name: St. Antony's Church Uvari
description: Perched dramatically on the sandy coastal dunes of the Gulf of Mannar in Uvari fishing village, a visually extraordinary Roman Catholic pilgrimage church dedicated to St. Antony of Padua, famed for its unique architectural design constructed in the exact shape of a giant Portuguese sailing vessel / caravel ship cutting through the coastal sands, attracting millions of interfaith pilgrims seeking blessings.

name: Javadi Hills & Vainu Bappu Observatory
description: Extending across Tirupattur and Tiruvannamalai districts at an average height of 3,800 feet, a picturesque forested sub-range of the Eastern Ghats known for sandalwood forests, tribal Malayali settlements, cascading waterfalls like Beemanmadavu Falls, and Kavalur village which houses the prestigious Vainu Bappu Observatory featuring a 2.34-meter optical reflecting telescope.

name: Yelagiri Hills & Swamimalai Trek
description: Perched at 3,600 feet in Tirupattur district, reached via 14 hairpin bends on a scenic ghat road, a tranquil cluster of 14 tribal mountain hamlets surrounded by rose gardens, orchards, and emerald valleys, famous for outdoor adventure activities like paragliding, boating on Punganoor Lake, and the popular trek to the highest peak, Swamimalai (4,338 ft).

name: Amaravathi Dam & Crocodile Farm Udumalpet
description: Constructed in 1957 across the Amaravathi River in the foothills of the Indira Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary (Anamalai Tiger Reserve) near Udumalpet, a 33-meter-high dam forming a scenic mountain lake surrounded by dense forests, celebrated for housing the largest wild mugger crocodile breeding and rehabilitation centre in South India.

name: Nanjarayan Bird Sanctuary Tiruppur
description: Covering 126 hectares around an 800-year-old historic irrigation tank constructed by King Nanjarayan of the Chola dynasty on the Noyyal River, designated as Tamil Nadu's 17th bird sanctuary in 2022 and an international Ramsar Wetland site in 2024, hosting over 130 bird species including Bar-headed Geese, Ruddy Shelducks, and painted storks.

name: Thirumoorthy Waterfall and Temple
description: Nestled at the base of the Anamalai hills near Udumalpet, featuring the sacred Sri Amanalingeswarar Temple dedicated to the Hindu Trinity (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva) and Panchalingam waterfall tumbling 30 meters down.

name: Thiruttani Murugan Temple (Thiruthanigai)
description: Perched at 700 feet atop Tanikai Hill in Tiruvallur district near the Andhra border, the fifth of the sacred six abodes (Arupadaiveedu) of Lord Murugan, revered as the peaceful hill where Lord Murugan cooled his anger after slaying Surapadman and wed his consort Goddess Valli, reached by climbing 365 steps representing the 365 days of the solar year.

name: Arunachaleswarar Temple & Girivalam Tiruvannamalai
description: Spread over 25 acres at the foot of the sacred Arunachala hill, one of the largest temple complexes in India representing the fire element (Agni Lingam), famous for four towering gopurams (Eastern Raja Gopuram at 217 ft) and the holy 14-km barefoot circumambulation path (Girivalam).

name: Muthupet Mangrove Forest & Lagoon
description: Spanning 12,000 hectares across the southernmost reaches of the Cauvery River delta on Palk Strait, one of the largest mangrove wetlands in southern India, dominated by Avicennia marina mangrove forests, featuring a scenic 1,500-meter wooden boardwalk traversing deep through root tangles into the vast Muthupet Lagoon where flamingos, herons, and mudskippers thrive.

name: Thyagaraja Temple Thiruvarur
description: Covering a colossal 33 acres in Thiruvarur, one of the most celebrated and historic temple complexes in Tamil Nadu dedicated to Lord Shiva as Somaskanda (Thyagaraja), famous for the massive 25-acre Kamalalayam temple tank (one of Asia's largest holy tanks), the legend of King Manu Needhi Chola who executed his own son under chariot wheels for killing a calf, and the world-famous 'Aazhi Ther' (the largest and heaviest wooden temple chariot in the world weighing 360 tonnes).

name: Vellore Fort & Jalakanteswarar Temple
description: Constructed in the 16th century CE by Vijayanagara chieftains Chinna Bommi Nayak and Thimma Reddy Nayak across 133 acres in Vellore, celebrated as one of the finest military granite fortresses in India, completely encircled by a colossal 191-foot-wide (58 m) and 29-foot-deep moat once teeming with 10,000 predatory crocodiles, housing the exquisitely sculpted Jalakanteswarar Shiva Temple, St. John's Church, and the Tipu Mahal.

name: Gingee Fort (Senji Fort / 'Troy of the East')
description: Spanning three formidable rocky granite hills (Rajagiri, Krishnagiri, and Chandrayandurg) interconnected by 13 kilometers of massive battlements, hailed by Chhatrapati Shivaji as the most impregnable fortress in India and dubbed the 'Troy of the East' by British general Arthur Wellesley, featuring the 7-storeyed Kalyana Mahal, royal grain granaries, cannon towers, and a 60-foot drawbridge.

name: Mandagapattu Cave Temple (Lakshitayatan)
description: Constructed around 600 CE by visionary Pallava King Mahendravarman I, historically celebrated as the earliest rock-cut stone cave temple in Tamil Nadu, marking the revolutionary transition from perishable brick and wood to living stone, bearing a famous Sanskrit foundation inscription stating it was carved without brick, timber, metal, or mortar for Brahma, Shiva, and Vishnu.

name: Krishnagiri Fort
description: One of the three dramatic citadel hills of the legendary Gingee Fort complex (termed the 'Troy of the East' by the British), crowned with ancient granaries, temples, and sheer stone ramparts.

name: Srivilliputhur Andal Temple
description: Constructed in the 8th century CE and renovated by Nayak and Pandya kings, one of the 108 Vaishnavite Divya Desams, celebrated as the sacred birthplace of the great Alwar poetess Andal (the only female Alwar) and her foster father Periyalwar, famous for its monumental 11-tiered 192-foot (59 m) Rajagopuram which is officially depicted on the State Emblem of Tamil Nadu.

name: Srivilliputhur Megamalai Tiger Reserve (SMTR)
description: Notified in February 2021 as India's 51st Tiger Reserve, combining the Grizzled Giant Squirrel Wildlife Sanctuary in Virudhunagar with the Megamalai Wildlife Sanctuary in Theni across 1,016 square kilometers of the Western Ghats, functioning as the primary catchment of the Vaigai River and home to tigers, elephants, leopards, and the arboreal Grizzled Giant Squirrel.
